messages:
liam (vendor-rel): Heads-up from Nebula: they sent an availability matrix and a note that reserved SKUs now have minimum commit windows of 90 days and monthly billing. Also called out sharp spot degradation during promotional periods.
julia (partnerships): can you drop their matrix? need numbers for the cost model
liam (vendor-rel): pasted CSV:
```csv
sku,region,type,commit_min_days,commit_granularity,spot_preempt_mean,sale_degradation_pct
nebula-gpu-a100,us-west,reserved,90,monthly,0.04,35
nebula-gpu-a100,us-east,spot,0,hourly,0.18,70
nebula-gpu-b200,eu-central,reserved,180,monthly,0.02,20
```
marcus (finance): 70% degradation? that's huge — we need to model tail risk vs average price, otherwise infra margins look better than reality
anya (prodops): For the cost model I'd like time-series of capacity churn if possible. ask them for 6 months of daily availability (how often pools shrink/expand).
liam (vendor-rel): requested yesterday. vendor replied: 'we can share a 6mo sample via signed link, redacted for customer names' — link they sent: https://nebula.example/samples/6mo-availability?token=REDACTED
sandra (marketplace): FYI marketplace listing changes can reduce spot pool size on short notice; add a volatility factor in the model (promo windows correlate with lower spot supply).
kyle (cost-model): suggested parameters to include in simulation:
```text
- committed_unit_cost
- spot_mean_cost
- spot_sd
- spot_degradation_percent_during_promos
- min_commit_days
- commit_billing_granularity
- lead_time_days_for_reserved_activation
```
marcus (finance): I'll run a sensitivity sweep. please make sure lead_time and min_commit flow into the cost function, otherwise reserved looks deceptively cheap when you ignore activation lag.
liam (vendor-rel): vendor also flagged 'bulk reserved discounts apply only at >500 GPU-months' — that's a clear cliff in pricing.
julia (partnerships): cliffs matter for Dedicated deals. marcus: can you produce two scenarios: cliff-triggered discount vs linear discount?
marcus (finance): on it. ETA EOD for a preliminary table.
anya (prodops): also confirm if committed capacity is strictly dedicated (no marketplace overlay). dedication vs blended availability changes utilization assumptions.
liam (vendor-rel): confirmed reserved == dedicated. marketplace == ephemeral. vendor may offer 'blended' only for multi-year bulk deals.
sandra (marketplace): recommend ops fallback rule: if spot pool falls below threshold, auto-fallback to smaller model or cached outputs to avoid latency SLO misses.
julia (partnerships): agree — add an ops toggle param to the rollout config for Dedicated customers.
liam (vendor-rel): follow-up questions I'm sending to vendor: (1) provide daily availability CSV for last 6 months (2) confirm cliff thresholds and discount bands (3) confirm lead_time for reserved activation in days (4) sample invoices for recent reserved purchases.
kyle (cost-model): ping me when they send invoices; I'll parse effective per-GPU-hour rates and billing granularity.
marcus (finance): once I run the sweep I'll push a small results table to the cost repo and link it here.
liam (vendor-rel): thanks. tagging @vendor-spindle-bot to record action: request_sent
vendor-spindle-bot: action recorded: request_sent by liam at 1845678901
julia (partnerships): next: prepare messaging for product about potential supply cliffs and Dedicated margin impact — cc: @product
sandra (marketplace): also loop legal for SLA language around marketplace volatility and promo-triggered spot drops.
liam (vendor-rel): will do. closing for now — I'll post the vendor dataset when it arrives.
